leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B023 prize (GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies). Five of the six name Drucker, Holst and Knudsen (El Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius); Perlmann names Drucker, Holst and Mojsov and would hold the citation to the physiology and the active peptide rather than the drug. Shared: the proglucagon-to-incretin-to-long-acting-agonist chain, independently confirmed outcome evidence, and the view that the third place is the open question. Not shared: whether Knudsen's acylated analogues or Mojsov's peptide identification is the third credit, and the citation wording (physiology only versus physiology plus long-acting therapy). Linnarsson states that he moved Knudsen into his trio in place of Mojsov after rereading colleagues' ballots.

areas_of_agreement: B023 is the sole configuration named by all six members, and each states that the opening unanimity is not itself the argument.
Drucker and Holst are named by all six members as the physiological core of B023.
The mechanism is regarded as stable and the clinical evidence as broad and independent (glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes), so no member raises maturity as a reason against B023.
All six members list attribution as the strongest reservation about B023, citing the three-person cap, the contested identification of GLP-1(7-36) and Habener's absence from the credited names.
All six members state that no candidate-specific conflict or recusal need is apparent.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should reward the physiological discovery only (Perlmann), the physiology plus the pharmacological solution to the short half-life (El Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius), or whether the compound is better framed as two achievements (raised by Linnarsson, Perlmann and Svenningsson).

Whether acylation and albumin-binding design is a discovery-level contribution (El Manira, Linnarsson, Svenningsson) or optimisation that makes the prize read as favouring a company (concern raised by El Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius as a reservation).

Among alternatives, B001 is named by five members (El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius), B051 by three (Linnarsson, Sandberg, Svenningsson), B022 by three (El Manira, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius) and B028 by one (Sandberg). Members differ on whether a mostly tool-based impact (B001) or a mechanistic pathway with limited clinical consequence (B051) is the stronger second achievement. These are alternatives, not preferred configurations.
Wahren-Herlenius adds that long-term safety of the incretin class beyond weight and glucose is still being defined; no other member raises this.
attribution_disputes: B023: priority for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is called contested by all six; Mojsov is credited by Perlmann only, and Habener (also Bell, per Perlmann) is outside the credited names. Several members state they cannot resolve it from the supplied record, and El Manira and Perlmann hold that unresolved priority argues against including Mojsov for now.

B023: Knudsen is a company-based development scientist; Perlmann, Linnarsson and El Manira regard her exclusion or inclusion as a real cost either way, and Sandberg says the third place depends on how the committee defines the core achievement.
B001: six credited claimants for three places, with Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck named by Linnarsson as hard to omit; El Manira and Perlmann doubt a three-name solution can be forced this year.
B022: Eshhar is not among the credited names (El Manira, Wahren-Herlenius).
B028: the unresolved Zhou priority question is raised by El Manira, who ranks it below CAR-T on that ground.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B023; more than a decade of outcome trials and global use is cited.
Perlmann states that delay carries a real cost for B023 because the laureates are living; no member contests this.

B001 is described as mature but with mostly research-tool impact on medicine (Linnarsson); B051 is described as having the least direct clinical consequence (Linnarsson, Sandberg). No member argues either is premature, but no member states a view on whether clinical consequence should weigh more heavily than conceptual advance in a second part.
Svenningsson notes that opening-stage unanimity may reflect the obviousness of impact more than a settled allocation.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: El Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann (stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons) and work in the same lamprey model system as Grillner; no credited candidate is involved and no recusal is proposed.
Linnarsson discloses eight recorded co-authored works with Sandberg (not independently audited); no credited candidate is involved and no recusal is proposed.
Perlmann discloses prior co-authorship with Ronald Evans, not a credited name on the shortlist, plus shared KI affiliation with colleagues; no recusal is proposed.
Sandberg discloses shared KI affiliation and past co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen on single-cell and neurogenesis work, not on the shortlist; no candidate tie is inferred.

Svenningsson (chair) discloses the Greengard postdoctoral period and roughly twenty co-authored works with Perlmann (not independently audited); neither concerns a shortlisted candidate and no recusal is proposed.

Wahren-Herlenius notes that B018 (cGAS-STING) is close to her interferon-related research field, with no documented personal tie to its credited names; she ranks it on common criteria. She lists co-authors Kuchroo and Sonesson, neither credited on the shortlist.
questions_for_round2: For B023, who holds the third place: Knudsen (five members) or Mojsov (Perlmann), and what documented evidence on identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide would settle priority among Mojsov, Habener and Bell?

Should the B023 citation reward the physiology, the development of long-acting therapies, or both, and does the committee accept a company-based development scientist alongside two academic discoverers?
If Knudsen and Mojsov cannot both be included, is a one-part B023 prize defensible as a compound of basic physiology and industrial development, or should the prize be split into two achievements?
Should B023 stand alone, or be paired with a second, distinct achievement? If so, which of B001, B051 or B022 is the strongest partner, and can its credit fit the three-person cap?
For B001, can a defensible three-name subset be drawn from Boyden, Bamberg, Nagel, Miesenboeck, Deisseroth and Hegemann, and who would be left out?
For B051, does the Mori and Walter pairing correctly divide early unfolded protein response credit, given Linnarsson's note that this rests on his recollection rather than the supplied record?
How much weight should established clinical benefit carry against conceptual advance and clean attribution when choosing a second part?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 configurations agree on one part, B023, and differ only in the third name (Knudsen in five, Mojsov in one) and in the citation's emphasis on discovery versus drug development. Members largely agree that attribution, not merit or maturity, is the open issue, and they rank alternatives differently; those alternatives are secondary positions and not counted as preferences. The disclosed collaborations are generic and none involves a shortlisted candidate. Round 2 needs to settle the third laureate and citation wording, and whether any second part is warranted.
